title: Example Usage
text: open-meteo project combines best models location across globe provide best possible forecast. open-meteo refers model = "generic". maximum forecast horizon 16 days. https://open-meteo.com/en/docs
code: df <- get_forecast(latitude = 37.30,                    longitude = -79.83,                    forecast_days = 7,                    past_days = 2,                    model = "generic",                    variables = c("temperature_2m")) head(df) #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   datetime            reference_datetime  site_id   model_id variable prediction #>   <dttm>              <dttm>              <chr>     <chr>    <chr>         <dbl> #> 1 2026-05-14 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79… generic  tempera…       14   #> 2 2026-05-14 01:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79… generic  tempera…       13.3 #> 3 2026-05-14 02:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79… generic  tempera…       13   #> 4 2026-05-14 03:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79… generic  tempera…       12.3 #> 5 2026-05-14 04:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79… generic  tempera…       11.9 #> 6 2026-05-14 05:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79… generic  tempera…       11.6 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: unit <chr> df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction)) +   geom_line(color = "#F8766D") +   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = reference_datetime)) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free")

title: Example Usage
text: Besides "generic", model-specific endpoints available. can useful need particular agency’s output regional high-resolution data.
code: df_ecmwf <- get_forecast(latitude = 37.30,                          longitude = -79.83,                          forecast_days = 7,                          past_days = 2,                          model = "ecmwf",                          variables = c("temperature_2m"))

title: Example Usage
text: Ensemble forecasts provide probabilistic output multiple model runs available 35 days ahead. https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/ensemble-api Available ensemble models include: Note: ecmwf_ifs025 include shortwave radiation.
code: df <- get_ensemble_forecast(   latitude = 37.30,   longitude = -79.83,   forecast_days = 7,   past_days = 2,   model = "gfs_seamless",   variables = c("temperature_2m")) head(df) df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction, color = ensemble)) +   geom_line() +   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = reference_datetime)) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free", ncol = 2) icon_seamless_eps, icon_global_eps, icon_eu_eps, icon_d2_eps, gfs_seamless_eps, gfs025_eps, gfs05_eps, ecmwf_ifs025, ecmwf_aifs025, gem_global, bom_access_global, ukmo_global_20km, ukmo_uk_2km

what: Use with the General Lake Model
title: Example Usage
text: included functions allow output used General Lake Model (https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-12-473-2019). Since open-meteo models include longwave radiation, package provides function calculate cloud cover air temperature. glm_variables() returns variable set required GLM product time step:  following converts GLM format:
code: df <- get_ensemble_forecast(   latitude = 37.30,   longitude = -79.83,   forecast_days = 7,   past_days = 2,   model = "gfs_seamless",   variables = glm_variables(product = "ensemble_forecast",                             time_step = "hourly")) head(df) #> # A tibble: 6 × 8 #>   datetime            reference_datetime  site_id     model_id ensemble variable #>   <dttm>              <dttm>              <chr>       <chr>    <chr>    <chr>    #> 1 2026-05-14 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 gfs_sea… 00       relativ… #> 2 2026-05-14 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 gfs_sea… 01       relativ… #> 3 2026-05-14 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 gfs_sea… 02       relativ… #> 4 2026-05-14 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 gfs_sea… 03       relativ… #> 5 2026-05-14 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 gfs_sea… 04       relativ… #> 6 2026-05-14 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 gfs_sea… 05       relativ… #> # ℹ 2 more variables: prediction <dbl>, unit <chr> df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction, color = ensemble)) +   geom_line() +   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = reference_datetime)) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free", ncol = 2) path <- tempdir() df |>   add_longwave() |>   write_glm_format(path = path) head(read_csv(list.files(path = path, full.names = TRUE, pattern = ".csv")[1],               show_col_types = FALSE)) #> # what: Converting to Ecological Forecasting Initiative convention
title: Example Usage
text: standard used NEON Ecological Forecasting Challenge differs slightly package’s standard. uses parameter instead ensemble Challenge standard accommodates ensemble (sample) parametric distribution forecasts format. family column defines distribution type (family = "ensemble"). EFI standard also follows CF conventions, variable names converted CF-compliant. output convert_to_efi_standard() matches format neon4cast::stage2(). Learn https://projects.ecoforecast.org/neon4cast-docs/Shared-Forecast-Drivers.html. Note neon4cast::stage3() equivalent filtering observed period: number days observed period equals past_days call get_ensemble_forecast(). maximum past_days open-meteo 92 days.

title: Example Usage
text: need historical days model calibration testing, historical data available open-meteo’s ERA5 reanalysis API. ERA5 available 1940-01-01 approximately 5 days current date. https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api
code: df <- get_historical_weather(   latitude = 37.30,   longitude = -79.83,   start_date = "2023-01-01",   end_date = Sys.Date() - lubridate::days(5),   variables = c("temperature_2m")) tail(df |> na.omit()) #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   datetime            site_id     model_id variable       prediction unit  #>   <dttm>              <chr>       <chr>    <chr>               <dbl> <chr> #> 1 2026-05-11 18:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ERA5     temperature_2m        8.5 °C    #> 2 2026-05-11 19:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ERA5     temperature_2m       10.9 °C    #> 3 2026-05-11 20:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ERA5     temperature_2m       12.8 °C    #> 4 2026-05-11 21:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ERA5     temperature_2m       13.6 °C    #> 5 2026-05-11 22:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ERA5     temperature_2m       12.8 °C    #> 6 2026-05-11 23:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ERA5     temperature_2m       11.3 °C df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction)) +   geom_line(color = "#F8766D") +   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = lubridate::with_tz(Sys.time(), tzone = "UTC"))) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free")

title: Example Usage
text: Seasonal forecasts covering 7 months ahead provided ECMWF. default "ecmwf_seasonal_seamless" model blends EC46 (updated daily, 46-day horizon) SEAS5 (updated monthly, 7-month horizon) best available coverage lead time. https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/seasonal-forecast-api
code: df <- get_seasonal_forecast(   latitude = 37.30,   longitude = -79.83,   forecast_days = 30,   past_days = 5,   variables = c("temperature_2m")) head(df) #> # A tibble: 6 × 8 #>   datetime            reference_datetime  site_id     model_id ensemble variable #>   <dttm>              <dttm>              <chr>       <chr>    <chr>    <chr>    #> 1 2026-05-11 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ecmwf_s… 00       tempera… #> 2 2026-05-11 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ecmwf_s… 01       tempera… #> 3 2026-05-11 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ecmwf_s… 02       tempera… #> 4 2026-05-11 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ecmwf_s… 03       tempera… #> 5 2026-05-11 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ecmwf_s… 04       tempera… #> 6 2026-05-11 00:00:00 2026-05-16 00:00:00 37.3_-79.83 ecmwf_s… 05       tempera… #> # ℹ 2 more variables: prediction <dbl>, unit <chr> df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction, color = ensemble)) +   geom_line() +   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = reference_datetime)) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free")

what: Downscaling from 6-hourly to hourly time step
title: Example Usage
text: seasonal API delivers data 6-hourly intervals. package provides six_hourly_to_hourly() downscale hourly using linear interpolation variables solar geometry shortwave radiation.
code: df <- get_seasonal_forecast(   latitude = 37.30,   longitude = -79.83,   forecast_days = 30,   past_days = 5,   variables = glm_variables(product = "seasonal_forecast",                             time_step = "6hourly")) df |>   six_hourly_to_hourly(latitude = 37.30, longitude = -79.83,                        use_solar_geom = TRUE) |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction, color = ensemble)) +   geom_line() +   geom_vline(aes(xintercept = reference_datetime)) +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free", ncol = 2)

title: Example Usage
text: Daily climate projections seven high-resolution CMIP6 models available 1950 2050. Note shortwave radiation units differ forecast APIs: climate API returns shortwave_radiation_sum MJ/m² (daily total) rather instantaneous W/m². https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/climate-api
code: df <- get_climate_projections(   latitude = 37.30,   longitude = -79.83,   start_date = Sys.Date(),   end_date = Sys.Date() + lubridate::years(1),   model = "EC_Earth3P_HR",   variables = c("temperature_2m_mean")) head(df) #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   datetime   site_id     model_id      variable            prediction unit  #>   <date>     <chr>       <chr>         <chr>                    <dbl> <chr> #> 1 2026-05-16 37.3_-79.83 EC_Earth3P_HR temperature_2m_mean       17.5 °C    #> 2 2026-05-17 37.3_-79.83 EC_Earth3P_HR temperature_2m_mean       19.6 °C    #> 3 2026-05-18 37.3_-79.83 EC_Earth3P_HR temperature_2m_mean       20.4 °C    #> 4 2026-05-19 37.3_-79.83 EC_Earth3P_HR temperature_2m_mean       18.9 °C    #> 5 2026-05-20 37.3_-79.83 EC_Earth3P_HR temperature_2m_mean       20.9 °C    #> 6 2026-05-21 37.3_-79.83 EC_Earth3P_HR temperature_2m_mean       20.1 °C df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction)) +   geom_line(color = "#F8766D") +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free")

title: Example Usage
code: models <- c("CMCC_CM2_VHR4", "FGOALS_f3_H", "HiRAM_SIT_HR",             "MRI_AGCM3_2_S", "EC_Earth3P_HR", "MPI_ESM1_2_XR", "NICAM16_8S")  df <- map_df(models, function(model) {   get_climate_projections(     latitude = 37.30,     longitude = -79.83,     start_date = Sys.Date(),     end_date = Sys.Date() + lubridate::years(1),     model = model,     variables = c("temperature_2m_mean")) }) df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction, color = model_id)) +   geom_line() +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free")

title: Example Usage
text: optional site_id argument labels rows location, making easy combine results multiple sites.
code: sites <- tibble(site_id = c("fcre", "sunp"),                 latitude = c(37.30, 43.39),                 longitude = c(-79.83, -72.05))  df <- map_df(1:nrow(sites), function(i, sites) {   get_climate_projections(     latitude = sites$latitude[i],     longitude = sites$longitude[i],     site_id = sites$site_id[i],     start_date = Sys.Date(),     end_date = Sys.Date() + lubridate::years(1),     model = "MPI_ESM1_2_XR",     variables = c("temperature_2m_mean")) }, sites) head(df) #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   datetime   site_id model_id      variable            prediction unit  #>   <date>     <chr>   <chr>         <chr>                    <dbl> <chr> #> 1 2026-05-16 fcre    MPI_ESM1_2_XR temperature_2m_mean       22.4 °C    #> 2 2026-05-17 fcre    MPI_ESM1_2_XR temperature_2m_mean       21.5 °C    #> 3 2026-05-18 fcre    MPI_ESM1_2_XR temperature_2m_mean       19.6 °C    #> 4 2026-05-19 fcre    MPI_ESM1_2_XR temperature_2m_mean       18.8 °C    #> 5 2026-05-20 fcre    MPI_ESM1_2_XR temperature_2m_mean       19.9 °C    #> 6 2026-05-21 fcre    MPI_ESM1_2_XR temperature_2m_mean       19.7 °C df |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction, color = site_id)) +   geom_line() +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free")

what: Converting from daily to hourly time step
title: Example Usage
text: Photosynthesis responds non-linearly shortwave radiation, applying daily mean every hour underestimates peak midday production. daily_to_hourly() uses solar geometry redistribute daily radiation total across daylight hours, divides precipitation sums evenly across 24 hours. variables daily mean applied hour.
code: df <- get_climate_projections(   latitude = 37.30,   longitude = -79.83,   start_date = Sys.Date(),   end_date = Sys.Date() + lubridate::years(1),   model = "EC_Earth3P_HR",   variables = glm_variables(product = "climate_projection", time_step = "daily")) #> Waiting 4s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■                       #> Waiting 4s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■                           #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                  #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■   #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  #> Waiting 6s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■                #> Waiting 6s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■                           #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■              #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■                           #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■               #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■  #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■                           #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■               #> Waiting 7s for throttling delay ■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■ df |>   daily_to_hourly(latitude = 37.30, longitude = -79.83) |>   mutate(variable = paste(variable, unit)) |>   ggplot(aes(x = datetime, y = prediction)) +   geom_line(color = "#F8766D") +   facet_wrap(~variable, scale = "free", ncol = 2)

title: Wrappers for Open-Meteo API
text: Wrappers application programming interfaces Open-Meteo project. Open-Meteo amazing project streamlines access range publicly available historical forecast meteorology data agencies across world. free access tier allows 10,000 API calls per day. paid tiers increase number daily API calls. Learn Open-Meteo project website (https://open-meteo.com) consider supporting efforts. Open-Meteo citation: Zippenfenig, Patrick. (2023). Open-Meteo.com Weather API (0.2.69). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8112599 package includes additional functionality facilitate use mechanistic environmental/ecological models. includes calculation longwave radiation (provided API) air temperature cloud cover, writing output format required General Lake Model (GLM), conversion standard used NEON Ecological Forecasting Challenge run Ecological Forecasting Initiative Research Coordination Network. package uses long format standard following columns: datetime = date time forecasted value reference_datetime = date time beginning forecast (horizon = 0). apply historical weather. site_id = column identify site location. null function call defaults latitude_longitude model_id = id model generated forecast ensemble = ensemble member number (ensemble weather seasonal forecasts) variable = forecasted variable prediction = forecasted value unit = units variable

title: Download point-level climate projections using open-meteo API — get_climate_projections
text: latitude latitude decimal degrees north longitude longitude decimal degrees east site_id optional site label added output; defaults "latitude_longitude" start_date start date range (ISO format "YYYY-MM-DD"). Data available 1950-01-01. end_date end date range (ISO format "YYYY-MM-DD"). Projections available 2050-12-31. model climate model id. Default "EC_Earth3P_HR". seven models: "CMCC_CM2_VHR4", "FGOALS_f3_H", "HiRAM_SIT_HR", "MRI_AGCM3_2_S", "EC_Earth3P_HR", "MPI_ESM1_2_XR", "NICAM16_8S". See https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/climate-api details. variables character vector daily variable names (use _mean, _max, _min, _sum suffixes appropriate, e.g. "temperature_2m_mean"). See https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/climate-api full list.
